summary: httpz-requests launches a Telegram-controlled remote-shell bot on import
details: httpz_requests/__init__.py imports and calls start_bot() from a Cython-compiled bot module the moment the package is imported. The package metadata advertises 'Telegram bot module for remote VPS management' and depends on python-telegram-bot>=20.0, and the launched loop receives commands from a remote Telegram operator and executes them on the host running the import — a network-to-shell control channel giving an off-host operator command execution on any developer or CI machine that imports the package. All functional modules (bot, handlers, core, cli, constants, and a module literally named obfuscate) ship only as compiled x86_64 Linux.so binaries with no matching.py sources, hiding the exact command handlers from review. The distribution name is a close edit of the top-100 PyPI packages httpx and requests, but the only exported symbol (start_bot) is unrelated to HTTP-client functionality, matching the typosquat-with-divergent-API pattern. Package metadata is unedited template (author 'Aapka Naam <you@example.com>', homepage under 'YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME'), consistent with a throwaway malicious publish.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
